problem.title: Find the Product's Neighborhood
problem.statement: Without calculating exactly, which number is closest to 49 × 203?
hints: Replace both factors with nearby friendly numbers.

validationMethods: Independent exact and distance audit: 49 × 203 = 9,947; its distances from choices A through E are 8,947, 4,947, 53, 40,053, and 90,053, so C is uniquely closest.
notes: The widely separated choices make estimation sufficient.

problem.title: Check the Display
problem.statement: A calculator display says 603 × 48 = 2,894. Which comparison proves that the displayed result is impossible?
hints: Replace each positive factor with a smaller friendly number.

solutionSteps.title: Build a lower bound
solutionSteps.body: Because 603 > 600 and 48 > 40, their product is greater than 600 × 40 = 24,000.

solutionSteps.title: Compare
solutionSteps.body: The displayed 2,894 is below 24,000, so it is impossible. Choice A gives the valid comparison.

validationMethods: Monotonic lower-bound proof: for positive factors, 603 > 600 and 48 > 40 imply 603 × 48 > 24,000, immediately excluding 2,894.
Independent exact and option audit: 603 × 48 = 603 × (50 − 2) = 30,150 − 1,206 = 28,944. Only choice A states a true comparison that proves the display impossible.
notes: The exact product is used only for independent validation, not required by the learner solution.

problem.title: Three Deliveries
problem.statement: A warehouse receives deliveries of 3,987, 2,014, and 1,002 items. Which number is closest to the total number of items received?
hints: Round each delivery to the nearest thousand before adding.

validationMethods: Independent exact and choice-distance audit: 3,987 + 2,014 + 1,002 = 7,003, only 3 from C and at least 997 from every other choice.
notes: This transfers magnitude control from products to a multi-addend sum.

problem.title: Hours in a Month
problem.statement: A 31-day month contains 24 hours per day. Which number is closest to the total number of hours in the month?
hints: Use 30 days as a nearby friendly number, and keep the unit hours.

solutionSteps.title: Choose the scale
solutionSteps.body: One extra day adds 24 hours, putting the exact total at 744 hours, closest to 750 hours.

validationMethods: Friendly-number estimate: 30 × 24 = 720 hours, which lies near 750 and far from the other choices.
Independent exact and distance audit: 31 × 24 = 744; its distance from 750 is 6, while its distances from 500 and 7,500 are 244 and 6,756, with the remaining choices farther still.
notes: The unit remains attached throughout the estimate and exact check.

problem.title: Trap a Product Between Bounds
problem.statement: Use 190 < 198 < 200 and 50 < 51 < 52. Which interval is guaranteed to contain 198 × 51?
hints: For positive numbers, multiply a lower bound by a lower bound and an upper bound by an upper bound.

solutionSteps.title: Find a lower bound
solutionSteps.body: Because 198 > 190 and 51 > 50, the product is greater than 190 × 50 = 9,500.

solutionSteps.title: Find an upper bound
solutionSteps.body: Because 198 < 200 and 51 < 52, the product is less than 200 × 52 = 10,400.

validationMethods: Positive-factor bound proof: 190 × 50 = 9,500 is a strict lower bound and 200 × 52 = 10,400 is a strict upper bound.
Independent exact and distractor audit: 198 × 51 = 198 × (50 + 1) = 9,900 + 198 = 10,098. It lies only in B; it falsifies C and D at their nearest endpoints and is far outside A and E.
notes: The supplied inequalities keep the challenge focused on magnitude reasoning rather than multiplication fluency.
